_about: Wisdom's sayings side by side (plan 7.6b): sayings of Job, Proverbs, Ecclesiastes and the Psalms, each beside the places that repeat it or take up its words, in the Law, the prophets, the Gospels and the letters, with what is alike and what differs. Every quotation machine-checked against the Berean; rows chosen and drafted by Claude Opus from the passages the theme map cites, the Berean editors' quotation notes and a search of the whole Berean; widened by the completeness search; every Alike and Different line read by the nine-reader panel (Sonnet). Takes no interpretive stance. A cell [verse, words, "aside"] is off the subject and shown, with an asterisk, for its shared words.
columns_note: Elsewhere in the Old Testament: the Law, the history books, the prophets and the Song of Solomon.

rows.title: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom

Job: the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom
Psalms: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom
Proverbs & Ecclesiastes: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge
The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom
The fear of the LORD is the instruction of wisdom

rows.alike: Psalm 111:10 and Proverbs 9:10 say in the same words "The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom"; Job 28:28 has "the fear of the Lord, that is wisdom".
rows.different: Proverbs 1:7 has "the beginning of knowledge" and Proverbs 15:33 "the instruction of wisdom". In Job 28:28 the words are said "to man"; Psalm 111:10 goes on "all who follow His precepts gain rich understanding", and Proverbs 9:10 "knowledge of the Holy One is understanding".

rows.title: Trust in the LORD; be not wise in your own eyes

Psalms: Commit your way to the LORD; trust in Him, and He will do it
Proverbs & Ecclesiastes: Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and lean not on your own understanding
in all your ways acknowledge Him, and He will make your paths straight
Be not wise in your own eyes; fear the LORD and turn away from evil
Do you see a man who is wise in his own eyes? There is more hope for a fool than for him
He who trusts in himself is a fool
Elsewhere in the Old Testament: Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes and clever in their own sight
blessed is the man who trusts in the LORD, whose confidence is in Him

rows.alike: Several speak of trusting the LORD: "trust in Him" (Psalm 37:5), "Trust in the LORD with all your heart" (Proverbs 3:5), "trusts in the LORD" (Jeremiah 17:7). Several speak of being wise in one's own eyes: "Be not wise in your own eyes" (Proverbs 3:7), "wise in his own eyes" (Proverbs 26:12), "wise in their own eyes" (Isaiah 5:21). Proverbs 3:5 puts "lean not on your own understanding" beside trust in the LORD, and Proverbs 28:26 says "He who trusts in himself is a fool".
rows.different: Proverbs 3:6 has "He will make your paths straight" and Psalm 37:5 "He will do it"; Jeremiah 17:7 calls the man who trusts in the LORD "blessed". Proverbs 26:12 says "There is more hope for a fool than for him", and Isaiah 5:21 begins "Woe".

rows.title: Guard your heart; out of the heart

Proverbs & Ecclesiastes: Guard your heart with all diligence, for from it flow springs of life
Gospels & Acts: the things that come out of the mouth come from the heart
out of the overflow of the heart the mouth speaks
The letters & Revelation: Philippians 4:7
the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your minds in Christ Jesus

rows.alike: Each speaks of the heart as kept or as the place things come from: "Guard your heart" (Proverbs 4:23) and "will guard your hearts" (Philippians 4:7); "from it flow springs of life" (Proverbs 4:23), "come from the heart" (Matthew 15:18), "out of the overflow of the heart the mouth speaks" (Luke 6:45).
rows.different: In Proverbs 4:23 the one addressed is told to guard the heart; in Philippians 4:7 it is "the peace of God" that "will guard your hearts and your minds". Proverbs 4:23 says "springs of life" flow from it; Matthew 15:18 says the things that come from the heart "defile a man", and Luke 6:45 speaks of "the good treasure" and "the evil treasure" of the heart.

rows.title: Naked from the womb, carrying nothing away

Job: Naked I came from my mother's womb, and naked I will return.
Psalms: when he dies, he will carry nothing away
Proverbs & Ecclesiastes: As a man came from his mother's womb, so he will depart again, naked as he arrived. He takes nothing for his labor to carry in his hands.
The letters & Revelation: 1 Timothy 6:7
we brought nothing into the world, so we cannot carry anything out of it

rows.alike: Job 1:21 and Ecclesiastes 5:15 both speak of coming from "mother's womb" and leaving "naked"; Ecclesiastes 5:15 ("He takes nothing for his labor"), Psalm 49:17 ("he will carry nothing away") and 1 Timothy 6:7 ("we cannot carry anything out of it") say nothing goes with him.
rows.different: Job speaks of himself and goes on "The LORD gave, and the LORD has taken away"; Ecclesiastes speaks of "a man" and "his labor", Psalm 49:17 adds "his abundance will not follow him down", and 1 Timothy 6:7 begins "we brought nothing into the world".

rows.title: The LORD disciplines the one He loves

Job: Blessed indeed is the man whom God corrects; so do not despise the discipline of the Almighty.
Psalms: Blessed is the man You discipline, O LORD
Proverbs & Ecclesiastes: My son, do not reject the discipline of the LORD, and do not loathe His rebuke
for the LORD disciplines the one He loves, as does a father the son in whom he delights.
Elsewhere in the Old Testament: just as a man disciplines his son, so the LORD your God disciplines you
The letters & Revelation: Hebrews 12:5
My son, do not take lightly the discipline of the Lord, and do not lose heart when He rebukes you.
Hebrews 12:6
For the Lord disciplines the one He loves, and He chastises every son He receives.
Hebrews 12:7
For what son is not disciplined by his father?
Revelation 3:19
Those I love I rebuke and discipline.

rows.alike: Proverbs 3:11-12 and Hebrews 12:5-6 both begin "My son", speak of "the discipline of the LORD" ("the discipline of the Lord" in Hebrews), and give the reason "the LORD disciplines the one He loves"; Proverbs 3:12 and Hebrews 12:7 set it beside a father and a son, and Deuteronomy 8:5 beside "a man" and "his son".
rows.different: Proverbs 3:11 says "do not reject" and "do not loathe His rebuke", where Hebrews 12:5 says "do not take lightly" and "do not lose heart when He rebukes you"; Proverbs 3:12 ends "as does a father the son in whom he delights", Hebrews 12:6 "He chastises every son He receives". Job 5:17 and Psalm 94:12 call the man disciplined "Blessed", and in Revelation 3:19 the speaker says it of himself: "Those I love I rebuke and discipline".

rows.title: He gives grace to the humble

Proverbs & Ecclesiastes: He mocks the mockers, but gives grace to the humble.
The letters & Revelation: James 4:6
God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble.
1 Peter 5:5
God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble.

rows.alike: All three end "gives grace to the humble".
rows.different: Proverbs 3:34 opens "He mocks the mockers"; James 4:6 and 1 Peter 5:5 open "God opposes the proud". James brings the words in with "This is why it says", and 1 Peter 5:5 after "clothe yourselves with humility toward one another, because".

rows.title: Love covers a multitude of sins

The letters & Revelation: James 5:20
cover over a multitude of sins
1 Peter 4:8
love covers over a multitude of sins

rows.alike: Proverbs 10:12 and 1 Peter 4:8 both say "love covers"; 1 Peter 4:8 and James 5:20 share "a multitude of sins".
rows.different: Proverbs 10:12 has "all transgressions" and sets it against "Hatred stirs up dissension"; 1 Peter 4:8 opens "Above all, love one another deeply"; in James 5:20 the one who covers sins is "Whoever turns a sinner from the error of his way", and love is not named.

rows.title: If your enemy is hungry

Proverbs & Ecclesiastes: If your enemy is hungry, give him food to eat, and if he is thirsty, give him water to drink.
For in so doing, you will heap burning coals on his head, and the LORD will reward you.
The letters & Revelation: Romans 12:20
If your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him a drink. For in so doing, you will heap burning coals on his head.

rows.alike: Both say "If your enemy is hungry" and "if he is thirsty", and both go on "For in so doing, you will heap burning coals on his head".
rows.different: Proverbs has "give him food to eat" and "give him water to drink", Romans "feed him" and "give him a drink"; Proverbs 25:22 ends "and the LORD will reward you", which Romans 12:20 does not have, and Romans opens "On the contrary".

rows.title: A dog returns to its vomit

Proverbs & Ecclesiastes: As a dog returns to its vomit, so a fool repeats his folly.
The letters & Revelation: 2 Peter 2:22
A dog returns to its vomit

rows.alike: Both have "a dog returns to its vomit".
rows.different: Proverbs 26:11 sets beside it "so a fool repeats his folly"; 2 Peter 2:22 counts it among "the proverbs" that "are true" and pairs it with "A sow that is washed goes back to her wallowing in the mud".

rows.title: Do not boast about tomorrow

Proverbs & Ecclesiastes: Do not boast about tomorrow, for you do not know what a day may bring.
The letters & Revelation: James 4:13
Today or tomorrow we will go to this or that city
James 4:14
You do not even know what will happen tomorrow!
James 4:16
you boast in your proud intentions. All such boasting is evil.

rows.alike: Both join boasting to "tomorrow" and answer it with what is not known: "you do not know what a day may bring" (Proverbs 27:1), "You do not even know what will happen tomorrow" (James 4:14).
rows.different: Proverbs 27:1 is one line; James gives the boast's own words, "Today or tomorrow we will go to this or that city", asks "What is your life?", and says "All such boasting is evil".

rows.title: He catches the wise in their craftiness

Job: He catches the wise in their craftiness
The letters & Revelation: 1 Corinthians 3:19
He catches the wise in their craftiness

rows.alike: The same words in both: "He catches the wise in their craftiness".
rows.different: Job 5:13 goes on "and sweeps away the plans of the cunning"; 1 Corinthians 3:19 brings the words in with "As it is written", after "the wisdom of this world is foolishness in God's sight".

rows.title: The LORD knows the thoughts of man, that they are futile

Psalms: The LORD knows the thoughts of man, that they are futile.
The letters & Revelation: 1 Corinthians 3:20
The Lord knows that the thoughts of the wise are futile.

rows.alike: Both say the Lord "knows" thoughts, and that they "are futile".
rows.different: Psalm 94:11 has "the thoughts of man", 1 Corinthians 3:20 "the thoughts of the wise"; 1 Corinthians brings the words in with "And again".

rows.title: Who has given, that He should repay him?

Job: Who has given to Me that I should repay him?
The letters & Revelation: Romans 11:35
Who has first given to God, that God should repay him?

rows.alike: Both ask who has given, that he should be repaid: "should repay him".
rows.different: Job 41:11 is in the first person, "to Me" and "I should repay", and goes on "Everything under heaven is Mine"; Romans 11:35 has "first given to God" and "God should repay".

rows.title: Like grass that withers, like a flower of the field

Job: Like a flower, he comes forth, then withers away
Psalms: they are like the new grass of the morning
by evening it fades and withers
My heart is afflicted, and withered like grass
his days are like grass-he blooms like a flower of the field
when the wind passes over, it vanishes
May they be like grass on the rooftops, which withers before it can grow
Elsewhere in the Old Testament: grass on the rooftops, scorched before it is grown
grass on the rooftops, scorched before it is grown
All flesh is like grass, and all its glory like the flowers of the field.
The grass withers and the flowers fall when the breath of the LORD blows on them; indeed, the people are grass.
The grass withers and the flowers fall, but the word of our God stands forever.
a son of man who withers like grass
The letters & Revelation: James 1:10
he will pass away like a flower of the field
James 1:11
withers the plant; its flower falls
1 Peter 1:24
All flesh is like grass, and all its glory like the flowers of the field; the grass withers and the flowers fall
1 Peter 1:25
but the word of the Lord stands forever.

rows.alike: Isaiah 40:6-8 and 1 Peter 1:24-25 share "All flesh is like grass, and all its glory like the flowers of the field", "the grass withers and the flowers fall" and a word that "stands forever"; Psalm 103:15 and James 1:10 both have "like a flower of the field", and 2 Kings 19:26, Isaiah 37:27 and Psalm 129:6 have "grass on the rooftops".
rows.different: Psalm 103:15 says it of "man", Psalm 102:11 the speaker of himself ("I wither away like grass"), Psalm 92:7 of "the wicked", Isaiah 51:12 of "a son of man" and James 1:10 of "the one who is rich"; Isaiah 40:8 has "the word of our God", 1 Peter 1:25 "the word of the Lord". Isaiah 66:14, "you will flourish like grass", uses the likeness for flourishing.

rows.title: Man is but a breath, a vapor

Job: my life is but a breath
my days are but a breath
Psalms: each man at his best exists as but a breath
surely each man is but a vapor
Lowborn men are but a vapor

rows.alike: Job 7:7, Job 7:16 and Psalm 39:5 say "but a breath", Psalm 39:11 and Psalm 62:9 "but a vapor", and Psalm 144:4 "Man is like a breath".
rows.different: In Job the speaker says it of himself, "my life" and "my days"; Psalm 39:5 and 39:11 say it of "each man", and Psalm 62:9 of "Lowborn men", setting beside them "the exalted are but a lie".

rows.title: Our days on earth are like a shadow

Job: our days on earth are but a shadow
like a fleeting shadow, he does not endure
Psalms: My days are like lengthening shadows
I am fading away like a lengthening shadow
his days are like a passing shadow
Proverbs & Ecclesiastes: he passes through his fleeting life like a shadow
their days will not lengthen like a shadow
Elsewhere in the Old Testament: Our days on earth are like a shadow, without hope.

rows.alike: 1 Chronicles 29:15 "Our days on earth are like a shadow" and Job 8:9 "our days on earth are but a shadow" are almost the same words; Psalm 144:4 has "his days are like a passing shadow" and Psalm 102:11 "My days are like lengthening shadows".
rows.different: 1 Chronicles 29:15 adds "without hope" and begins "we are foreigners and strangers in Your presence"; Job 8:9 begins "we were born yesterday and know nothing"; Ecclesiastes 6:12 asks "who knows what is good for a man", and Ecclesiastes 8:13 says of the wicked that "their days will not lengthen like a shadow".

rows.title: A thousand years like a day

Psalms: in Your sight a thousand years are but a day that passes, or a watch of the night
The letters & Revelation: 2 Peter 3:8
With the Lord a day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years are like a day.

rows.alike: Both set "a thousand years" beside "a day".
rows.different: Psalm 90:4 is spoken to God, "in Your sight", and adds "or a watch of the night"; 2 Peter 3:8 says "With the Lord" and gives it both ways, "a day is like a thousand years" as well.

rows.title: Their voice has gone out into all the earth

Psalms: their voice has gone out into all the earth, their words to the ends of the world.
The letters & Revelation: Romans 10:18
Their voice has gone out into all the earth, their words to the ends of the world.

rows.alike: The same words in both: "their voice has gone out into all the earth, their words to the ends of the world".
rows.different: Psalm 19:4 goes on "In the heavens He has pitched a tent for the sun"; Romans 10:18 gives the words as the answer to "did they not hear? Indeed they did".

rows.title: Whoever would love life and see good days

Psalms: Who is the man who delights in life, who desires to see good days?
Keep your tongue from evil and your lips from deceitful speech.
Turn away from evil and do good; seek peace and pursue it.
The eyes of the LORD are on the righteous, and His ears are inclined to their cry.
But the face of the LORD is against those who do evil, to wipe out all memory of them from the earth.
Turn away from evil and do good
The letters & Revelation: 1 Peter 3:10
Whoever would love life and see good days must keep his tongue from evil and his lips from deceitful speech.
1 Peter 3:11
He must turn from evil and do good; he must seek peace and pursue it.
1 Peter 3:12
For the eyes of the Lord are on the righteous, and His ears are inclined to their prayer. But the face of the Lord is against those who do evil.

rows.alike: Both run in the same order: "see good days", the tongue kept "from evil" and the lips "from deceitful speech", "do good", "seek peace and pursue it", eyes "on the righteous", ears "inclined to their" cry or prayer, and the face "against those who do evil". Psalm 37:27 has "Turn away from evil and do good" as well.
rows.different: Psalm 34:12 asks "Who is the man who delights in life", where 1 Peter 3:10 says "Whoever would love life"; the Psalm's commands ("Keep your tongue", "Turn away") are "must" in 1 Peter; "their cry" in Psalm 34:15 is "their prayer" in 1 Peter 3:12, and Psalm 34:16 goes on "to wipe out all memory of them from the earth", which 1 Peter does not have.

rows.title: Not one of his bones will be broken

Psalms: He protects all his bones; not one of them will be broken.
Elsewhere in the Old Testament: you may not break any of the bones
or break any of its bones
Gospels & Acts: Not one of His bones will be broken.

rows.alike: Psalm 34:20 has "not one of them will be broken" and John 19:36 "Not one of His bones will be broken"; Exodus 12:46 and Numbers 9:12 forbid breaking "any of the bones" or "any of its bones".
rows.different: Exodus 12:46 and Numbers 9:12 are commands, and Numbers 9:12 is about the Passover ("They must observe the Passover according to all its statutes"); Psalm 34:20 says "He protects all his bones"; John 19:36 brings its words in with "so that the Scripture would be fulfilled".

rows.title: Taste and see that the LORD is good

Psalms: Taste and see that the LORD is good
The letters & Revelation: 1 Peter 2:3
you have tasted that the Lord is good

rows.alike: Both speak of tasting "that the LORD is good" ("that the Lord is good" in 1 Peter).
rows.different: Psalm 34:8 calls on the hearer, "Taste and see", and goes on "blessed is the man who takes refuge in Him"; 1 Peter 2:3 says of those it addresses "now that you have tasted".

rows.title: He has scattered abroad his gifts to the poor

Psalms: He has scattered abroad his gifts to the poor; his righteousness endures forever
The letters & Revelation: 2 Corinthians 9:9
He has scattered abroad His gifts to the poor; His righteousness endures forever.

rows.alike: Psalm 112:9 and 2 Corinthians 9:9 share "scattered abroad", "gifts to the poor" and "righteousness endures forever"; Psalm 111:3 and Psalm 112:3 have "righteousness endures forever" as well.
rows.different: Psalm 112:9 adds "his horn will be lifted high in honor"; 2 Corinthians 9:9 brings the words in with "As it is written". Psalm 111:3 has the words beside "Splendid and majestic is His work", Psalm 112:3 beside "Wealth and riches are in his house".

rows.title: Make a level path for your feet

Proverbs & Ecclesiastes: Make a level path for your feet
The letters & Revelation: Hebrews 12:13
Make straight paths for your feet

rows.alike: Both say "Make" a path "for your feet".
rows.different: Proverbs 4:26 has "a level path" and goes on "all your ways will be sure"; Hebrews 12:13 has "straight paths" and gives the reason "so that the lame may not be disabled, but rather healed".

rows.title: If the righteous, how much more the ungodly and the sinner

Proverbs & Ecclesiastes: If the righteous receive their due on earth, how much more the ungodly and the sinner!
The letters & Revelation: 1 Peter 4:18
If it is hard for the righteous to be saved, what will become of the ungodly and the sinner?

rows.alike: Both open with "If", name "the righteous", and end with "the ungodly and the sinner".
rows.different: Proverbs 11:31 has the righteous who "receive their due on earth" and says "how much more"; 1 Peter 4:18 has "If it is hard for the righteous to be saved" and asks "what will become of" the rest.

rows.title: Better to be told, "Come up here!"

Proverbs & Ecclesiastes: Do not exalt yourself in the presence of the king, and do not stand in the place of great men
it is better to be told, “Come up here!” than to be demoted in the presence of the prince
Gospels & Acts: do not sit in the place of honor
in humiliation, you will have to take the last place
Friend, move up to a better place

rows.alike: Both warn against taking a high place ("the place of great men", "the place of honor") and set being called up ("Come up here!", "Friend, move up to a better place") against being put lower ("demoted", "in humiliation").
rows.different: Proverbs 25:6-7 is set before "the king" and "the prince"; Luke 14:8-10 at "a wedding banquet" with a "host", and Luke 14:10 adds "you will be honored in front of everyone at the table with you".

rows.title: Do not move an ancient boundary stone

Proverbs & Ecclesiastes: Do not move an ancient boundary stone which your fathers have placed.
Do not move an ancient boundary stone or encroach on the fields of the fatherless
Elsewhere in the Old Testament: You must not move your neighbor's boundary marker, which was set up by your ancestors
Cursed is he who moves his neighbor's boundary stone.
like those who move boundary stones

rows.alike: All speak of moving a boundary stone (in Deuteronomy 19:14, a "boundary marker"); Deuteronomy 19:14 "set up by your ancestors" and Proverbs 22:28 "which your fathers have placed" both name who set it.
rows.different: Deuteronomy 19:14 says "your neighbor's" and 27:17 "his neighbor's", and 27:17 adds "Cursed is he who moves"; Proverbs says "ancient", and 23:10 adds "the fields of the fatherless"; Job 24:2 sets it beside "they pasture stolen flocks"; Hosea 5:10 says it of "The princes of Judah".

rows.title: They will inherit the land

Psalms: his descendants will inherit the land
those who hope in the LORD will inherit the land
But the meek will inherit the land
Surely those He blesses will inherit the land
The righteous will inherit the land and dwell in it forever.
He will raise you up to inherit the land
Elsewhere in the Old Testament: he will enable Israel to inherit the land
enable them to inherit the land that you will see
he who seeks refuge in Me will inherit the land
Gospels & Acts: Blessed are the meek, for they will inherit the earth.

rows.alike: Each has "inherit the land" or, in Matthew 5:5, "inherit the earth"; Psalm 37:11 "the meek will inherit the land" and Matthew 5:5 "the meek, for they will inherit the earth" both name the meek.
rows.different: They name who inherits: "those who hope in the LORD" (Psalm 37:9), "those He blesses" (37:22), "The righteous" (37:29), "his descendants" (Psalm 25:13), "he who seeks refuge in Me" (Isaiah 57:13); in Deuteronomy 1:38 Joshua will "enable" Israel to inherit it, and in 3:28 "enable them". Matthew 5:5 has "the earth" and opens "Blessed are".

rows.title: He will repay each one according to his deeds

Job: according to a man's deeds He repays him
Psalms: He has repaid me according to the cleanness of my hands.
Repay them according to their deeds
You will repay each man according to his deeds.
the LORD has repaid me according to my righteousness, according to the cleanness of my hands
Proverbs & Ecclesiastes: Will He not repay a man according to his deeds?
I will repay the man according to his work.
Elsewhere in the Old Testament: May the LORD repay the evildoer according to his evil!
He has repaid me according to the cleanness of my hands.
rewarding him according to his righteousness
repay each man according to all his ways, since You know his heart
rewarding him according to his righteousness
repay each man according to all his ways, since You know his heart
He will repay according to their deeds
to reward a man according to his way, by what his deeds deserve
I will repay them according to their deeds
to reward each one according to his ways and according to the fruit of his deeds
Repay her according to her deeds
I will judge you according to your ways and repay you for all your abominations
I will judge you according to your ways and repay you for all your abominations
repay him according to his deeds
the LORD has repaid me according to my righteousness, according to my cleanness in His sight
Gospels & Acts: He will repay each one according to what he has done
The letters & Revelation: Romans 2:6
will repay each one according to his deeds
1 Corinthians 3:8
each will be rewarded according to his own labor
2 Timothy 4:14
The Lord will repay him according to his deeds.
Revelation 2:23
I will repay each of you according to your deeds
Revelation 22:12
to give to each one according to what he has done

rows.alike: Psalm 62:12 "You will repay each man according to his deeds", Proverbs 24:12 "repay a man according to his deeds", Romans 2:6 "will repay each one according to his deeds" and Revelation 2:23 "repay each of you according to your deeds" are nearly the same words; 1 Kings 8:39 and 2 Chronicles 6:30 have "repay each man according to all his ways".
rows.different: Some are prayers ("May the LORD repay the evildoer", 2 Samuel 3:39; "Repay them according to their deeds", Psalm 28:4), some questions ("Will He not repay", Proverbs 24:12), and in 2 Samuel 22:21, Psalm 18:20, 2 Samuel 22:25 and Psalm 18:24 the speaker says of himself "He has repaid me according to the cleanness of my hands" or "the LORD has repaid me according to my righteousness". Matthew 16:27 says it of "the Son of Man", and Revelation 22:12 "My reward is with Me"; in Proverbs 24:29 a man is told not to say "I will repay the man according to his work".

rows.title: Like a tree planted by streams of water

Psalms: Blessed is the man who does not walk in the counsel of the wicked
He is like a tree planted by streams of water, yielding its fruit in season, whose leaf does not wither
Elsewhere in the Old Testament: blessed is the man who trusts in the LORD
He is like a tree planted by the waters that sends out its roots toward the stream.
like a vine in your vineyard, planted by the water

rows.alike: Both say "blessed is the man" and go on "He is like a tree planted by" water, with leaves that stay fresh ("whose leaf does not wither"; "its leaves are always green") and fruit that keeps coming ("yielding its fruit in season"; "nor does it cease to produce fruit").
rows.different: Psalm 1:1 names the man by what he does not do, "does not walk in the counsel of the wicked", Jeremiah 17:7 by "who trusts in the LORD"; Jeremiah 17:8 adds "It does not fear when the heat comes" and "a year of drought". Ezekiel 19:10 says "planted by the water" of "a vine", "Your mother".

rows.title: There is no one who does good, not even one

Psalms: There is no one who does good.
to see if any understand, if any seek God
All have turned away, they have together become corrupt; there is no one who does good, not even one.
There is no one who does good.
to see if any understand, if any seek God
All have turned away, they have together become corrupt; there is no one who does good, not even one.
no one alive is righteous before You
Proverbs & Ecclesiastes: there is no righteous man on earth who does good and never sins
Elsewhere in the Old Testament: there is no one who does not sin
there is no one who does not sin
The letters & Revelation: Romans 3:10
There is no one righteous, not even one.
Romans 3:11
There is no one who understands, no one who seeks God.
Romans 3:12
All have turned away, they have together become worthless; there is no one who does good, not even one.

rows.alike: Psalm 14:3, Psalm 53:3 and Romans 3:12 share "All have turned away, they have together become" and "there is no one who does good, not even one"; Ecclesiastes 7:20 has "no righteous man on earth who does good and never sins", and 1 Kings 8:46 and 2 Chronicles 6:36 "there is no one who does not sin".
rows.different: Where the Psalms have "become corrupt", Romans 3:12 has "become worthless"; Psalms 14:2 and 53:2 have God looking "to see if any understand, if any seek God", where Romans 3:11 says "There is no one who understands, no one who seeks God". Romans 3:10 brings its words in with "As it is written" and begins "There is no one righteous"; 1 Kings 8:46 and 2 Chronicles 6:36 set the words inside "When they sin against You".

rows.title: Blessed is he whose transgressions are forgiven

Psalms: Blessed is he whose transgressions are forgiven, whose sins are covered.
Blessed is the man whose iniquity the LORD does not count against him
The letters & Revelation: Romans 4:7
Blessed are they whose lawless acts are forgiven, whose sins are covered.
Romans 4:8
Blessed is the man whose sin the Lord will never count against him.

rows.alike: Both say "Blessed" of those whose wrongs "are forgiven" and "whose sins are covered", and of "the man" whom the Lord does not "count against him".
rows.different: Psalm 32:1 has "transgressions", Romans 4:7 "lawless acts"; Psalm 32:2 says "does not count" and goes on "in whose spirit there is no deceit", where Romans 4:8 says "will never count" and stops there.

rows.title: In favor with God and man

Proverbs & Ecclesiastes: Then you will find favor and high regard in the sight of God and man.
Elsewhere in the Old Testament: in favor with the LORD and with man
Gospels & Acts: Jesus grew in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and man.
The letters & Revelation: 2 Corinthians 8:21
not only in the eyes of the Lord, but also in the eyes of men

rows.alike: 1 Samuel 2:26 "in favor with the LORD and with man", Proverbs 3:4 "favor and high regard in the sight of God and man" and Luke 2:52 "in favor with God and man" join favor with God and with man; 2 Corinthians 8:21 has "in the eyes of the Lord" and "in the eyes of men".
rows.different: 1 Samuel 2:26 and Luke 2:52 say it of one who grew ("the boy Samuel", "Jesus"), both with "stature" and Luke adding "wisdom"; Proverbs 3:4 says to the one addressed "Then you will find favor"; 2 Corinthians 8:21 is about "taking great care to do what is right".
